rationale:
Evidence: iteration 5 (kp 2.0, ki 0.3, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.0, search_right, 12 mm sensors at x = -0.04, -0.015, 0, 0.015, 0.04) is the best raced design at 75.779. Every raced run has ended with exactly one line-loss event and max_error of 0.061 to 0.067 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, while steering_oscillation stays low (0.10 to 0.16). The failure is a slow drift to one edge, not weaving. Sensor_size 0.016 lowered progress (iteration 7), and kp 1.6 and 2.5 both lost progress (iterations 4 and 6), so those are rejected.

Change: I revert sensor_size to 0.012 and change one field from the best design, kd 0.1 to 0.2, to add derivative damping against the slow drift. This is the candidate the Evaluator approved (entityR1), so it races unchanged.

Expected result: progress near iteration 5 (oval about 0.29, s-bend about 0.15, slalom about 0.11), with max_error falling toward or below 0.06 m and line_loss_events still 1 or lower. Steering oscillation should stay near or below 0.16.

Decision rules for the next iteration: (1) If progress matches or exceeds iteration 5 and max_error falls, keep kd 0.2 and test base_speed 1.1 with search_right and kp 2.0. (2) If progress falls or oscillation rises clearly above 0.16, revert kd to 0.1 and test base_speed 1.1 from there. (3) If max_error stays near 0.063 m on every track whatever kd does, damping is not the limit, so stop tuning kd and test base_speed alone with the iteration 5 gains.

Hypotheses: H11, the drift is a slow approach to the edge that extra derivative action damps. H13, speed trades progress between the oval and the bend tracks, so base_speed 1.1 may add progress on the bends. Measurements wanted: progress, max_error, line_loss_events and steering_oscillation per track, and whether the loss point moves along the course.
